description: This bar chart, from the paper "Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning Design Spaces," illustrates the performance of various fine-tuning methods on a metric labeled "BLEU Performance," with the vertical axis scaled linearly from 86 to 88. The horizontal axis lists the fine-tuning methods, including "LoRA," "BitFit," "S₁-model," "S₄-model," and "S₅-model," arranged in a non-alphabetical order that appears to follow a descending trend in performance for the "large" model. Each method is represented by a pair of stacked bars, with the legend indicating that blue bars correspond to the "base" RoBERTa size and orange bars to the "large" RoBERTa size. The chart visually emphasizes that for most methods, the "large" model outperforms the "base" model, with the "S₅-model" showing the highest performance for both sizes, reaching approximately 88.0 for the "large" model and around 87.5 for the "base" model. The "BitFit" method shows the lowest performance, with the "base" model at approximately 86.0 and the "large" model at around 86.5. The bars are not sorted, and no additional visual emphasis such as shading or bolding is applied beyond the color coding in the legend.
